youtube.title: How Did CUDA Turn Nvidia Into a Giant?
youtube.description:
In 2006 Nvidia put a feature called CUDA into every graphics card it sold, and for years almost no gamer used it. Profits fell into losses and the share price fell more than 80 percent. So why did Nvidia keep paying for it?

This documentary follows the decision from a Stanford student's side project to the Toronto lab that trained a breakthrough AI on two gaming cards, and to the first company worth five trillion dollars. Every figure is on screen with its source.

{CHAPTERS}

sources.claim: On 29 October 2025 Nvidia became the first company worth five trillion dollars
Founded in April 1993 by three engineers who planned it at a Denny's in San Jose
sources.source: Nvidia corporate history page; Tae Kim, The Nvidia Way (W. W. Norton, Dec 2024)

sources.claim: Fiscal 2007 revenue just over $3.07 billion, net income $449 million
sources.source: Nvidia Form 10-K, fiscal year ended 28 Jan 2007

sources.claim: AMD agreed to buy ATI for $5.4 billion in 2006
Ian Buck built the Brook language for GPUs at Stanford
sources.source: Buck et al., 'Brook for GPUs', SIGGRAPH 2004

sources.claim: Buck joined Nvidia in 2004
sources.source: Nvidia executive biography of Ian Buck

sources.claim: GeForce 8800 GTX and CUDA announced 8 November 2006; launch price $599; fastest card of its day
sources.source: Nvidia press release, 8 Nov 2006; AnandTech review, 8 Nov 2006

sources.claim: 681 million transistors, 128 stream processors, unified architecture replacing separate fixed units
G80 die about 484 square millimetres
CUDA lets programmers write C code for the GPU
First public CUDA toolkit February 2007; version 1.0 June 2007
sources.source: Nvidia CUDA release notes, Feb 2007 and Jun 2007

sources.claim: Tesla cards for scientists launched in 2007
CUDA kept on every GeForce card from the 8 series on; Huang's account of the reasoning (installed base, developers follow hardware people own) and of investor questions
sources.source: Jensen Huang, Acquired podcast interview, Oct 2023; Stratechery interview, Mar 2022; Tae Kim, The Nvidia Way, 2024

sources.claim: Cost of CUDA carried by Nvidia through larger chips and engineering effort on tools
sources.source: Tae Kim, The Nvidia Way, Dec 2024

sources.claim: University of Illinois named the first CUDA Center of Excellence in 2008
ATI showed its own low-level GPU route, Close to Metal, in 2006
OpenCL 1.0 published December 2008, proposed by Apple through the Khronos Group
Nvidia also supported OpenCL
July 2008: Nvidia said some laptop chips were failing and took a charge of $150-200 million
sources.source: Nvidia Form 8-K and press release, 2 Jul 2008

sources.claim: Shares fell about 30 percent the next day after the charge and a lowered forecast
September 2008: about 360 jobs cut, roughly 6.5 percent of the workforce
Net income: FY2008 $798M, FY2009 loss $30M, FY2010 loss $68M, FY2011 $253M
Share price fell more than 80 percent from its 2007 high to late 2008
sources.source: Nasdaq historical prices, Oct 2007 to Nov 2008

sources.claim: Intel described Larrabee in 2008 and in December 2009 said it would not ship as a consumer product
sources.source: Seiler et al., SIGGRAPH 2008; Intel statement, 4 Dec 2009

sources.claim: Tianhe-1A, with 7,168 Nvidia GPUs, world's fastest in November 2010
Titan at Oak Ridge used 18,688 Nvidia GPUs and topped the list in November 2012
sources.source: TOP500 list, Nov 2012; Oak Ridge National Laboratory

sources.claim: AlexNet trained on two GTX 580 cards in five to six days, programmed with CUDA
sources.source: Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton, 'ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks', NIPS 2012

sources.claim: GTX 580 launched at $499
Top-5 error 15.3 percent versus 26.2 percent for the next best entry
sources.source: ILSVRC 2012 results; Krizhevsky et al., NIPS 2012

sources.claim: 'All of our experiments suggest that our results can be improved simply by waiting for faster GPUs and bigger datasets to become available.'
Google's 2012 network used 1,000 machines with 16,000 cores; Stanford matched it with three GPU machines
sources.source: Le et al., ICML 2012; Coates et al., 'Deep learning with COTS HPC systems', ICML 2013

sources.claim: cuDNN released in 2014 and adopted by the main deep learning frameworks
sources.source: Nvidia developer blog, Sep 2014; Chetlur et al., arXiv, Oct 2014

sources.claim: DGX-1 unveiled April 2016 at $129,000
Huang hand-delivered the first DGX-1 to OpenAI in August 2016; inscription 'To the future of computing and humanity'
sources.source: Nvidia blog, Aug 2016; photo of the signed unit, Aug 2016

sources.claim: ChatGPT launched November 2022; trained on a Microsoft supercomputer of tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs
Passed Intel in market value July 2020; $1T May 2023; $2T Feb 2024; $4T July 2025; $5T October 2025
sources.source: Reuters, 8 Jul 2020, 30 May 2023, 23 Feb 2024, 9 Jul 2025, 29 Oct 2025

sources.claim: More than four million developers use CUDA
AMD is building its own GPU software, ROCm, to compete
